target: Mi ha domandato perché non fossi venuto alla sua festa.
english: He asked me why I hadn't come to his party.
old: "Perche" in reported questions: "perche non sei venuto" → "perche non fossi venuto".
focus: Fix accents (perché) and say it plainly: reported questions after domandare can take subjunctive – 'non fossi venuto'.

target: Ha detto che sarebbe venuto alla festa di sabato sera.
english: He said he would come to the party on Saturday night.
old: Future becomes conditional in reported speech: "verro" → "sarebbe venuto".
focus: Fix 'verrò' accent and stress that Italian uses the PAST conditional 'sarebbe venuto' where English says plain 'would come'.

target: Mi ha scritto che sarebbe tornato non appena avesse finito.
english: He wrote me that he would return as soon as he had finished.
old: "Non appena" + pluperfect subjunctive in subordinate clause of reported speech.
focus: Plain words, no 'subordinate clause': in the past, 'as soon as he had finished' becomes 'non appena avesse finito', pairing with 'sarebbe tornato'.

target: Di soldi, ne ha fin troppi ma non è per niente felice.
english: As for money, he has far too much but isn't happy at all.
old: Topicalization with resumptive pronoun "ne" restates the fronted topic.
focus: Drop 'topicalization/resumptive pronoun' – plain: front the topic with di, echo it with ne: 'Di soldi, ne ha fin troppi'.

target: Che Dio ti benedica per quello che hai fatto!
english: May God bless you for what you have done!
old: Independent subjunctive for wishes and exhortations: Che + subjunctive.
focus: Anchor 'Che Dio ti benedica' – che + subjunctive = 'may...'; plain words, drop 'independent subjunctive/exhortations'.

target: Che sia chiaro a tutti: non tollero ritardi.
english: Let it be clear to everyone: I don't tolerate delays.
old: "Che sia" introduces an exhortative subjunctive in independent clauses.
focus: Plain words: 'Che sia chiaro' = let it be clear – che + subjunctive can issue a directive, not just a wish; drop 'exhortative/independent clauses'.

target: Sembra che abbiano già preso una decisione.
english: It seems they have already made a decision.
old: Congiuntivo passato after 'sembra che'.
focus: 'Sembra che' + subjunctive – anchor 'abbiano già preso'; seeming = uncertainty, hence subjunctive; plain words, not 'congiuntivo passato'.

target: Sembra che la squadra abbia bisogno di un nuovo allenatore.
english: It seems the team needs a new coach.
old: Subjunctive after "che": the congiuntivo expresses uncertainty, opinion, wish, or evaluation.
focus: Sembra che takes subjunctive (abbia) – impressions count as uncertainty even when they feel factual; anchor on this card's sembra che / abbia, drop the four-item trigger list.

target: Bisogna che il cuoco prepari il menu per la festa.
english: The cook needs to prepare the menu for the party.
old: Impersonal necessity + "che" triggers the subjunctive: "Bisogna che tu studi."
focus: Bisogna che + subjunctive – quote THIS card's 'Bisogna che il cuoco prepari', not the stock 'Bisogna che tu studi'; plain words, no 'impersonal necessity'.

target: Bisogna che io prenoti il volo prima che i prezzi aumentino.
english: I need to book the flight before prices go up.
old: These conjunctions always trigger the subjunctive: a meno che (unless), prima che (before), senza che (without).
focus: Prima che + aumentino – 'before' clauses take subjunctive because the event hasn't happened yet; anchor on this card, drop the a-meno-che/senza-che list (dup on 2 cards, must differ).

target: È il film più bello che io abbia mai visto.
english: It's the most beautiful film I have ever seen.
old: Superlative relative (il piu... che) triggers subjunctive.
focus: 'The most beautiful ever' takes subjunctive: il più bello che io abbia mai visto – lead with the surprise, not 'superlative relative'; fix 'piu' accent.

target: Voglio che tutti in famiglia si sentano amati e apprezzati.
english: I want everyone in the family to feel loved and appreciated.
old: Verbs of opinion/wish/doubt + "che" require the congiuntivo. This is one of Italian's signature features.
focus: Voglio che + si sentano – Italian can't say 'want someone to do'; wants about other people need che + subjunctive. Cut the trigger list and 'signature features' fluff.

target: Questo libro, l'ho già letto almeno tre volte con piacere.
english: This book, I've already read it at least three times with pleasure.
old: Left dislocation: topic moved to front, resumed by pronoun "l'".
focus: Questo libro, l'ho già letto – the fronted topic gets echoed by l', and the echo pronoun is required, not sloppy speech. No 'left dislocation'.

target: Sarà stato mezzanotte quando finalmente siamo rientrati a casa.
english: It must have been midnight when we finally got back home.
old: Future perfect of probability: "sara stato" = it must have been.
focus: Sarà stato mezzanotte = 'it must have been midnight' – future tense as a guess about the past; lead with the surprise and fix the 'sara' accent.

target: Essendo stanco, ha deciso di rimandare il lavoro a domani.
english: Being tired, he decided to postpone the work until tomorrow.
old: Gerund clause (essendo + adjective/past participle) for causal subordination.
focus: Essendo stanco – a fronted gerund means 'since/because': 'being tired' = because he was tired. Plain words, no 'causal subordination'.

target: Non è che non voglia venire; è che non posso proprio.
english: It's not that I don't want to come – it's that I really can't.
old: "Non e che" + subjunctive for negating a presupposition.
focus: Non è che non voglia – 'it's not that I don't...' softens a denial and takes subjunctive; fix the 'Non e che' accent, drop 'negating a presupposition'.

target: Ne ha combinate di tutti i colori.
english: He's been up to all sorts of mischief.
old: "Combinarne di tutti i colori" = to get up to all sorts of mischief. "Ne" is a partitive pronoun here – "of them/of it."
focus: Ne ha combinate di tutti i colori – literally 'pulled off ones of every color' = every kind of mischief. One rule: keep the idiom's literal logic, cut the 'partitive pronoun' lesson.

target: Non avendo ricevuto risposta, ho deciso di chiamare direttamente.
english: Not having received a reply, I decided to call directly.
old: Compound gerund (avendo + past participle) for completed prior action.
focus: Non avendo ricevuto = 'not having received' – avendo + participle packs the earlier event into one clause, like English 'having done'. No 'compound gerund' lead.

target: Pur sapendo la verità, ha preferito non dire nulla.
english: Despite knowing the truth, he preferred not to say anything.
old: "Pur" + gerund = although/despite doing something (concessive gerund).
focus: Pur sapendo la verità = 'despite knowing the truth' – pur flips a gerund into 'although'. Anchor sapendo from this card (tip is duplicated on 2 cards, must differ); cut '(concessive gerund)'.

target: È auspicabile che si trovino soluzioni condivise al più presto.
english: It is desirable that shared solutions be found as soon as possible.
old: "E auspicabile che" is formal academic/political register.
focus: È auspicabile che + si trovino – bureaucratic 'it is hoped that', takes subjunctive; gloss auspicabile and fix the 'E' accent.

target: Arrivato a casa, si è messo subito a cucinare la cena.
english: Having arrived home, he immediately started cooking dinner.
old: Past participle clause (participio passato) replaces a temporal subordinate clause.
focus: Arrivato a casa = 'once he'd arrived home' – a bare past participle can open the sentence, no 'having' word needed. Quote the card; no 'participio passato' lead.

target: Vale la pena sottolineare l'importanza di questo risultato scientifico.
english: It is worth emphasizing the importance of this scientific result.
old: "Vale la pena sottolineare" is a formal hedging expression in academic writing.
focus: Vale la pena sottolineare – literally 'it's worth the pain to underline'; standard academic emphasis formula. It's emphasis, NOT hedging – fix that.

target: Quanto più ci penso, tanto meno capisco.
english: The more I think about it, the less I understand.
old: Correlative comparatives: "Più... più..." = The more... the more. "Più studio, più imparo" = The more I study, the more I learn.
focus: Quanto più ci penso, tanto meno capisco = 'the more I think, the less I understand' – anchor the card's own quanto/tanto pair; drop the 'Più studio, più imparo' stock example.

target: È proprio questo che volevo dire durante la nostra discussione.
english: This is exactly what I wanted to say during our discussion.
old: Cleft sentence: "E ... che" focuses emphasis on the highlighted element.
focus: È proprio questo che volevo dire – the è...che frame spotlights one element ('THIS is what I meant'). Plain words, no 'cleft sentence'; fix the 'E' accent.

target: Imparare una lingua richiede tempo, pazienza e molta costanza.
english: Learning a language requires time, patience, and great consistency.
old: Infinitive clause as subject: "Imparare una lingua" functions as the subject.
focus: Imparare una lingua = 'learning a language' – Italian uses the infinitive where English uses -ing as a subject. Lead with the English contrast, drop the circular 'functions as the subject'.

target: Sia che piova sia che splenda il sole, io esco.
english: Whether it rains or the sun shines, I'm going out.
old: 'Sia che...sia che' with subjunctive.
focus: Sia che piova sia che splenda = 'whether it rains or shines' – both halves take subjunctive. Gloss it and give the hook; current tip is a naked fragment.

target: Di pazienza, ne servirà molta per portare a termine questo.
english: We'll need a lot of patience to see this through.
old: Topicalization: "Di pazienza" is fronted; "ne" resumes it in the clause.
focus: Di pazienza, ne servirà molta – 'of patience' fronted, then echoed by ne. Plain words, no 'topicalization'; different angle from the l' card (it-3424).

target: Il suo continuo lamentarsi mi da un enorme fastidio quotidiano.
english: His constant complaining greatly annoys me every day.
old: Nominalized infinitive: "il lamentarsi" = the act of complaining (functions as noun).
focus: Il suo continuo lamentarsi – the infinitive works as a noun and takes il, suo, and adjectives: 'his constant complaining'. No 'nominalized infinitive' lead.

target: Letta la lettera, ha capito finalmente la gravita della situazione.
english: Having read the letter, he finally understood the gravity of the situation.
old: "Letta la lettera" = avendo letto la lettera (implicit subject must match main clause).
focus: Letta la lettera – the opening participle AGREES with its noun (letta, feminine) and means 'having read the letter'. The agreement is the gem; cut 'implicit subject must match'.

target: Il vivere in città ha i suoi vantaggi ma anche svantaggi.
english: Living in the city has its advantages but also disadvantages.
old: "Il vivere" = nominalized infinitive used as subject.
focus: Il vivere in città – Italian can put 'il' on an infinitive to make it a noun subject: 'living in the city'. Article angle (distinct from it-3596 and it-3640); no 'nominalized infinitive' lead.

target: Ciò premesso, si procede alla votazione.
english: With that said, we proceed to the vote.
old: Participial construction: using a past participle as a clause. "Finito il lavoro, uscì" = Having finished the work, he went out. Common in formal Italian.
focus: Anchor in THIS card: 'Ciò premesso' = 'that having been stated' – a past participle standing alone as a whole clause in formal Italian; drop the borrowed Finito-il-lavoro example.

target: Fermo restando il rispetto delle norme vigenti.
english: While maintaining respect for existing regulations.
old: Absolute participial clause: "Detto questo, passiamo oltre" = That said, let's move on. The participle has its own implied subject. Formal/written.
focus: 'Fermo restando' is literally 'remaining firm' – a frozen legal/formal opener meaning 'without prejudice to'; quote this card, not Detto questo.

target: L'aver studiato all'estero mi ha dato una prospettiva diversa.
english: Having studied abroad gave me a different perspective.
old: Compound nominalized infinitive: l'aver + past participle.
focus: 'L'aver studiato' = 'the having studied' – Italian puts l' before an infinitive to turn it into a noun where English uses -ing; give a hook, cut 'compound nominalized infinitive'.

target: Per quanto la questione possa sembrare irrilevante, merita attenzione.
english: However irrelevant the issue may seem, it deserves attention.
old: Complex concessive clause with 'per quanto' + subjunctive.
focus: 'Per quanto' = 'however much' and always drags the verb into the subjunctive (possa sembrare); say the rule, not just the label.

target: Bisogna che io studi di più per l'esame.
english: I need to study more for the exam.
old: Impersonal expression of necessity + "che" always requires the subjunctive mood.
focus: 'Bisogna che' + subjunctive (io studi) – and bisogna is subjectless: 'io bisogno' doesn't exist; quote bisogna itself, not just 'che'.

target: Mica male questo posto!
english: This place is not bad at all!
old: 'Mica' is an emphatic negation.
focus: 'Mica male' = 'not bad at all' – colloquial mica strengthens or, as here, entirely replaces non; quote the card and add the gloss.

target: Senza che nessuno se ne accorgesse, il tempo era passato.
english: Without anyone noticing, time had passed.
old: Senza che + imperfect subjunctive (se ne accorgesse): negative result clause.
focus: 'Senza che' takes the subjunctive (se ne accorgesse) – and Italian stacks it with nessuno where English says 'anyone'; lead with that trap.

target: L'azienda per la quale mia madre ha lavorato per vent'anni ha chiuso i battenti.
english: The company my mother worked for twenty years closed down.
old: Combines formal relative (per la quale) + time expression.
focus: 'Per la quale' is the formal written cousin of 'per cui' – la quale agrees with l'azienda; make the register contrast the point, drop the 'combines' framing.

target: Avendo finito il lavoro, uscì.
english: Having finished work, he left.
old: Gerundio passato for completed prior actions.
focus: 'Avendo finito' = 'having finished' – avendo + participle marks an action completed before the main verb; plain words, no 'gerundio passato' label.

target: Purché venga fatta giustizia, accetterò qualsiasi verdetto.
english: As long as justice is done, I'll accept any verdict.
old: Purché + subjunctive (venga fatta): formal conditional clause with passive.
focus: 'Purché' = 'provided that' and always takes the subjunctive (venga fatta); give the gloss first, cut 'formal conditional clause with passive'.

target: Lungi dall'essere risolto, il problema si è aggravato.
english: Far from being resolved, the problem has worsened.
old: Lungi da + infinitive: formal/literary expression of distance from a state.
focus: 'Lungi dall'essere' = 'far from being' – lungi is an archaic 'far' that survives only in this formal formula; add the literal gloss.

target: Ce la metto tutta.
english: I'm giving it my all.
old: 'Mettercela tutta' means to give it one's all.
focus: 'Ce la metto tutta' – ce and la are frozen parts of mettercela tutta ('put it all there'); la points at nothing, and that's the trap; don't just re-translate.

target: Ho fatto riparare la macchina.
english: I had the car repaired.
old: Fare + infinitive for causative constructions.
focus: 'Ho fatto riparare' = 'I made repair' – fare + infinitive means someone else did it for you, Italian's standard way to 'get X done'.

target: Non ce la faccio più!
english: I can't take it anymore!
old: 'Farcela' is a common idiomatic pronominal verb.
focus: 'Non ce la faccio più' – farcela = to manage/cope; ce and la are fixed inside the verb, and più supplies the 'anymore'.

target: Se la prende per tutto.
english: He gets upset about everything.
old: 'Prendersela' means to take offense.
focus: 'Se la prende' – prendersela = to get upset/take it personally; add con for the target: se la prende con me.

target: Andando avanti così, non finiremo mai.
english: Going on like this, we'll never finish.
old: Gerundio for manner: "Rispose ridendo" = He answered laughing. The gerund (-ando/-endo) describes how an action is performed.
focus: Re-anchor on THIS card: 'andando avanti così' – the bare gerund covers English 'if/by going on like this' with no word for if or by; drop the Rispose-ridendo example.
